title: API: POST /api/portfolio/positions
description: Implement the route body in app/api/routers/portfolio.py (currently a 501 stub). Route signature and schemas (PositionIn/PositionOut) are already wired.

checklist.step: Route signature + PositionIn/PositionOut schemas already defined
Decide and document duplicate-ticker behavior (merge vs reject) — flagged as an open decision in docs/architecture/API.md's Error Cases section
Implement handler: insert/update PositionORM, return 201 with the created/updated position
Write integration test covering create, and the decided duplicate-ticker behavior
Run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing and confirm no regression

decisions.decision: Duplicate-ticker add merges into the existing position rather than rejecting with 409/422: quantity is summed, avg_cost_basis becomes the quantity-weighted average of the existing and incoming cost bases, and entry_date keeps the earlier of the two dates. Ticker matching is case-insensitive (input is normalized to uppercase before lookup/storage). The response is always 201 (matching the route's existing status_code=201), whether the request created a new row or merged into one. current_price/unrealized_pnl_pct are always returned as null from this endpoint — price enrichment happens on read (GET /api/portfolio via the not-yet-built data-cache), not on write.
decisions.rationale: Merge was chosen over reject for three reasons: (1) API.md's endpoint description already calls this 'Add or update a position (manual entry / CSV-import row)' — 'or update' signals update/merge semantics, not a hard reject; (2) the primary real-world use case (buying more shares of a stock already held, or re-importing an updated CSV) is exactly what a brokerage's own position tracking does via weighted-average cost basis — rejecting would force the client to first GET the existing position, hand-compute the merge, DELETE, then re-POST, pushing merge logic onto every caller instead of doing it once in the API; (3) a 409 reject provides no real safety benefit here since there's no data loss risk in merging (the alternative, tracking separate cost-basis lots per ticker, isn't in the API.md response shape — PositionOut has one avg_cost_basis per ticker, so multiple lots aren't representable and rejecting wouldn't change that limitation, it would just require the client to do the same weighted-average math instead of the server). Rejected alternative: reject with 409 Conflict, requiring the client to DELETE then re-POST to update a position — this was the closest competitor but adds friction for the common case (averaging up/down) with no corresponding benefit, and the docs don't hint at wanting per-lot tracking. Case-insensitive ticker normalization was a secondary judgment call in the same spirit: 'AAPL' and 'aapl' referring to different positions would be a confusing surprise, and every other example ticker in the docs is uppercase.

decisions.decision: Added a FastAPI lifespan hook in app/main.py that runs Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) on startup, as a stopgap until the separate db-migrations task (Alembic) lands.
decisions.rationale: Without it, POST /api/portfolio/positions (and any other DB-backed route) would fail with 'no such table: positions' against a fresh SQLite file, since nothing in the codebase currently creates the schema outside of test fixtures that build their own in-memory engine. db-migrations (docs/tasks/db-migrations.json) is explicitly a separate, not-yet-done task scoped to Alembic setup, and isn't a dependency of this task, so building full migration tooling here would be out of scope. create_all is idempotent and only creates tables that don't already exist, so it's safe to leave in place after db-migrations ships (Alembic's own upgrade path will simply find the tables already present, matching the standard 'stamp head' pattern for retrofitting Alembic onto an existing create_all-based schema) — rejected alternative was leaving the endpoint non-functional against a real (non-test) database until db-migrations is picked up, which would make this task's own deliverable not actually work end-to-end.

decisions.decision: Fixed the blocking ZeroDivisionError (PR #17 review) by adding Field(gt=0) to both PositionIn.quantity and PositionIn.avg_cost_basis in app/api/schemas.py, rather than adding a defensive check in the router handler. Also added regression tests covering zero/negative quantity, zero/negative avg_cost_basis, and the specific duplicate-ticker-quantity-cancels-to-zero scenario from the review (all now 422, not 500).
decisions.rationale: Rejecting non-positive quantity/cost-basis at the schema layer is a strict improvement over a router-level guard: it produces FastAPI's standard 422 validation-error shape for free (consistent with every other invalid-body case), it documents the constraint directly in the OpenAPI schema so API consumers see it without reading the handler, and it eliminates the ZeroDivisionError at its root rather than special-casing merged_quantity == 0 in the merge arithmetic (a targeted `if merged_quantity == 0: raise HTTPException(422, ...)` guard was considered and rejected — it would only catch the exact-cancellation case the reviewer found, not the broader problem that quantity/avg_cost_basis were never meant to be negative or zero in the first place, e.g. a negative avg_cost_basis would otherwise still be silently accepted). A negative-quantity 'reduce a position' operation was also considered and rejected as out of scope: docs/architecture/API.md's Error Cases section and the route's own docstring already state there is no partial-quantity-reduction endpoint (delete and re-add instead), so this endpoint has never supported negative quantities as a feature — the missing constraint was a gap, not an intentionally permissive design.

decisions.decision: Added unique=True to PositionORM.ticker (app/db/models.py) to close the TOCTOU gap flagged as non-blocking in the PR #17 review, but did not add explicit IntegrityError handling in the router for the resulting rare concurrent-insert-collision case.
decisions.rationale: The constraint itself is a clean, one-line, low-risk change: there's no Alembic migration to retrofit yet (schema is still produced by the create_all stopgap — see the other decision below), and every existing insert path already normalizes tickers to uppercase before the lookup/write, so no existing test or code path relies on two rows sharing a ticker. Stopped short of also catching the resulting IntegrityError (e.g. retry-as-merge) because that's materially more logic (a retry loop or a transaction-level upsert) for a race that requires two concurrent requests for a brand-new ticker to interleave between the existing SELECT and INSERT — genuinely low-probability against the current single-process/single-worker uvicorn setup the review itself called out as low risk, and worth its own focused change (with its own tests) rather than folding into this fix-round. Net effect of doing only the constraint: the race, if it ever happens, now surfaces as a loud 500 (IntegrityError) instead of silently creating two rows for one ticker and breaking the merge invariant — a strict improvement even without the retry handling, and the retry handling is deferred, not abandoned.

decisions.decision: Documented the create_all lifespan stopgap as an explicit interim state in docs/architecture/Backend.md §7, and added a checklist item plus a description note to docs/tasks/db-migrations.json flagging that a fresh install already has tables from create_all, so db-migrations needs `alembic stamp head` (not a blind `alembic upgrade head`) against such a database.
decisions.rationale: Addresses the PR #17 review's third (non-blocking) comment directly: the interim state was previously only recorded in this task's own decisions array, which whoever picks up db-migrations wouldn't necessarily read before starting. Putting it in Backend.md (the doc db-migrations.json's own references field points to) and in db-migrations.json's own checklist/description makes it discoverable from the two places that task will actually be read from.

decisions.decision: Fixed the second-round blocking finding (Field(gt=0) doesn't reject Infinity, so a merged NaN avg_cost_basis crashed db.commit() with an unhandled IntegrityError) by adding allow_inf_nan=False to both PositionIn.quantity and PositionIn.avg_cost_basis in app/api/schemas.py. While reproducing it, found and fixed a second, previously-latent bug the fix itself exposed: Pydantic's finite_number validation error echoes the raw rejected value back in its `input` field, and FastAPI's default RequestValidationError handler hands that straight to Starlette's JSONResponse, which renders with json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False) — serializing a literal inf/nan there raises an unhandled ValueError *inside the error handler itself*, so the client got a raw 500 with no body, not the intended 422, even with the schema fix in place (confirmed directly with TestClient(raise_server_exceptions=False)). Fixed by registering a RequestValidationError exception handler in app/main.py that recursively sanitizes non-finite floats in the (already jsonable-encoded) error body to their string form before responding, preserving FastAPI's default {"detail": [...]} shape. Also addressed the non-blocking ticker validation comment: added min_length=1 plus a field_validator that strips whitespace and rejects blank/whitespace-only tickers, since it was a clean, low-risk fix in the same file already being touched, and directly protects the documented merge invariant (a whitespace-padded ticker like ' AAPL ' previously created a second row instead of merging).
decisions.rationale: allow_inf_nan=False was chosen over a custom lt=float('inf')/gt=float('-inf') Field constraint (which wouldn't reject NaN, since NaN compares false to every ordering operator including its own gt/lt bounds) or a custom field_validator (more code for something Pydantic already has a dedicated, well-tested constraint for). The response-serialization crash was not in either reviewer's reported comment, but was surfaced by writing a regression test that checked the actual response (not just the status code) for the Infinity case reported in the fix suggestion — treating 'fix the schema gap' as 'make the whole request/response round-trip correctly for this input,' consistent with the task's instruction to look for adjacent failure modes in the same gap rather than patching narrowly. Sanitizing to a string (rather than e.g. dropping the input field, or rounding to a large finite float) was chosen because it keeps the error message informative and both changes are strictly additive to the existing {"detail": [...]} shape FastAPI clients already expect, so no existing 422 consumer breaks. Ticker min_length + strip was implemented as flagged (non-blocking, judgment call was whether to do it now vs defer): done now since the docs/architecture/Backend.md-documented merge invariant is directly undermined by the gap and the fix is small and localized; the field_validator raises ValueError on a strip-to-empty ticker (e.g. ' ') so that whitespace-only tickers 422 alongside the empty-string case caught by min_length=1, rather than silently creating a blank-ticker position.

decisions.decision: A real human (GitHub user "rainoko", not the raino-agent automation account) answered the round-3 upper-bound-vs-finite-check question directly on PR #17 with: "cant there be guard for that. doesnt pyhton have bigdecimal like java. maybe numpy helps". Interpreted as: add a guard (validate before commit, matching option (b) from the original question) and prefer Python's arbitrary-precision decimal.Decimal for the merge arithmetic over native float64 -- decimal.Decimal is the actual Python equivalent of Java's BigDecimal. numpy was explicitly not adopted: numpy's float32/float64 types have the exact same silent-overflow-to-inf/nan characteristics as native Python floats (they're the same IEEE-754 binary representation), so substituting numpy would not close the gap the human is asking about -- it would just relocate the same bug. No upper bound (Field(le=...)) was added on quantity/avg_cost_basis, since the human's comment reads as endorsing a guard/precision fix over picking an arbitrary business-specific ceiling, and pinning a realistic maximum position size in the OpenAPI contract remains exactly the kind of product call the original question flagged as not decidable from the docs -- the human's answer resolves the mechanism question (guard + Decimal, not more special-casing) without taking a position on a numeric ceiling, so introducing one now would be reading more into the comment than it said.
decisions.rationale: Recorded verbatim per the orchestrator's explicit instruction to quote the human PR comment before acting on it, and to keep the audit trail of why a hard numeric ceiling was still not introduced even though it remains one of the two originally-offered options -- so a future reader of this task doesn't wonder why option (a) was seemingly ignored.

decisions.decision: Implemented the merge-arithmetic overflow fix using decimal.Decimal internally only, inside add_position's merge branch (app/api/routers/portfolio.py) -- not as a change to the PositionIn/PositionOut Pydantic schema field types, which remain float. The merged quantity and avg_cost_basis are computed as Decimal (constructed from the existing/incoming floats), then converted back to float and checked with math.isfinite() before being assigned to the ORM row or committed; a non-finite result raises HTTPException(422, ...) with a plain-string ErrorDetail-shaped body (matching the existing stocks.py 422 pattern) instead of reaching db.commit() at all. Deliberately did not wrap the Decimal construction/division in a try/except DecimalException backstop: by the time this code runs, both operands are already-validated finite floats (the existing row's stored values, and the incoming request's schema-validated allow_inf_nan=False/gt=0 fields), so Decimal construction can't raise, the divisor can't be zero, and Decimal's own exponent range vastly exceeds anything a float64 input could produce -- an except branch here would be dead code, untestable without contriving an input that can't actually occur, which is worse for the 90% branch-coverage gate than not having it.
decisions.rationale: Chose internal-only Decimal over changing the schema field types to Decimal/str for three reasons: (1) JSON has no native arbitrary-precision decimal type -- a schema-level Decimal would either serialize as a plain JSON number (round-tripping through float on the wire anyway, defeating the purpose) or as a string (a breaking API/OpenAPI contract change requiring the frontend to parse decimal strings, disproportionate to a merge-arithmetic edge case); (2) the underlying PositionORM columns are SQLAlchemy Float (float64) -- even a perfectly precise Decimal merge result still has to be stored as, and read back as, a float64, so the representable-range ceiling is set by the storage layer regardless of what type the arithmetic happens in, meaning Decimal's real benefit here is precision/reliability of the computation (no silent inf/nan from float64's own arithmetic, e.g. the (inf*a+b*c)/inf=nan pattern from round 2, and no precision loss when averaging widely-different-magnitude cost bases), not an increase in what can ultimately be stored; (3) confirmed directly that Decimal does not make the final float64 conversion raise on overflow either (float(Decimal(1e308)+Decimal(1e308)) still silently evaluates to inf, not an exception) -- so an explicit finite check after conversion is required either way, and is what actually turns the failure into a clean 422 rather than a raw 500, which is the real guard being asked for. Considered and rejected: comparing the raw Decimal merge result against Decimal(sys.float_info.max) before converting (equivalent behavior, more code, no different outcome from checking math.isfinite() on the converted float); adding Field(le=...) upper bounds instead of/alongside this (deferred per the decision above -- the human's comment reads as endorsing the guard-plus-Decimal approach, not asking for a hard ceiling, and picking one is still a product call this task isn't positioned to make unilaterally).

questions.question: PR #17 has hit 3 rounds of needs_work on the same underlying failure family (unbounded/non-finite numeric input in the duplicate-ticker merge path causing float overflow -> NaN -> an unhandled 500 on commit). Rounds 1-2 fixed the exact-cancellation ZeroDivisionError and the directly-submitted Infinity/NaN cases; round 3 found that two individually-valid large finite floats (e.g. quantity=avg_cost_basis=1e308 posted twice for the same ticker) still overflow inside the merge arithmetic itself, after validation passes. What's the right stopping point here: (a) add a hard upper bound (Field(le=...)) on quantity/avg_cost_basis with a specific realistic maximum you're comfortable pinning in the OpenAPI contract, (b) validate the *computed* merged values are finite right before commit and 422 if not (no upper bound needed, but doesn't produce as informative an error for the caller), or (c) something else? This is a product/API-contract call (what's a legitimate maximum position size/cost basis for this app) that isn't decidable from docs/Analyse.md or docs/architecture/API.md alone.
questions.context: Raised by the orchestrator per orchestrate-tasks' 3-round retry cap, to avoid dispatching a 4th fix round without a steer on where the numeric-bounds line should actually be drawn.

comments.summary: Blocking (round 3, new): Field(gt=0, allow_inf_nan=False) on PositionIn.quantity/avg_cost_basis rejects a directly-submitted non-positive/non-finite value, but places no upper bound on magnitude. Two individually-valid finite floats can still overflow during the merge arithmetic in add_position (existing.quantity + position.quantity, and the weighted-average division) -- Python float arithmetic overflows silently to inf/nan rather than raising. Reproduced live: POST {ticker: AAPL, quantity: 1e308, avg_cost_basis: 1e308, entry_date: ...} -> 201 (both fields individually finite/positive, pass validation cleanly). A second identical POST for the same ticker (merge path) -> unhandled 500: merged_quantity overflows to inf, avg_cost_basis computes to nan, and db.commit() raises sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError: NOT NULL constraint failed: positions.avg_cost_basis (sqlite3 binds the NaN parameter as NULL, tripping the NOT NULL column). Neither round-2 fix (schema-level allow_inf_nan=False, or the RequestValidationError sanitizing handler in app/main.py) covers this path -- no RequestValidationError is ever raised here since both inputs pass validation individually; the non-finite value is produced after validation, inside the router's own merge arithmetic, and nothing re-validates the computed merged_quantity/avg_cost_basis before they're assigned to the row and committed. Fix suggestion: add a realistic upper bound (le=...) to quantity/avg_cost_basis in the schema, and/or validate the computed merged values are finite before assigning/committing (422, not a raw 500), plus a regression test posting two large-but-individually-valid finite floats for the same ticker.

Re-confirmed clean (no further gaps in the same family, per the dispatched adversarial re-hunt): direct NaN (not just Infinity) for both quantity and avg_cost_basis is already tested (test_nan_quantity_returns_422, test_nan_avg_cost_basis_returns_422) and reconfirmed passing; negative infinity is confirmed rejected (gt=0 alone already excludes it, and allow_inf_nan=False would reject it independently either way); no other numeric field in schemas.py has the same gap -- PositionIn.quantity/avg_cost_basis are the only client-supplied numeric inputs anywhere in the schema module, every other float field (OHLCVBar, TideScreen/WaveScreen/Indicators, Equity, RiskPosition/RiskResponse, PositionOut) belongs to a response-only model never parsed from a request body.

Non-blocking, re-surfaced by the code-review skill this round (not new, already flagged non-blocking in round 2 and covered by this task's create_all stopgap decision record): unique=True on PositionORM.ticker is only applied by create_all to a table it creates from scratch -- against a pre-existing SQLite file whose positions table predates this PR, create_all won't retroactively ALTER it to add the constraint, so the TOCTOU-closing unique index silently doesn't take effect there. Worth folding into docs/architecture/Backend.md's existing interim-state note (currently only discusses CREATE TABLE failing on re-run, not a missed ALTER on an already-existing table) when db-migrations picks this up.

Blocking (new in this fix round): Field(gt=0) on PositionIn.quantity/avg_cost_basis rejects zero/negative but not Infinity (float('inf') > 0 is True in Python/Pydantic), so the merge arithmetic can still crash with an unhandled 500 -- the same failure class the fix round set out to eliminate, just reached via a different input than the exact-cancellation case that's now fixed. Reproduced independently: POST quantity=Infinity is accepted (201, and the response silently serializes quantity back as null -- data loss), then a second same-ticker POST with a finite quantity computes merged_quantity=inf and avg_cost_basis=(inf*a+b*c)/inf=nan; SQLite rejects binding NaN into the NOT NULL avg_cost_basis column, raising an unhandled sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError out of db.commit() with no rollback and no ErrorDetail body. Fix suggestion: Field(gt=0, lt=float('inf')) (or a finite-float validator) plus a regression test for an Infinity/NaN quantity or cost basis.

RESOLVED (was blocker in the prior review pass): the originally-reported ZeroDivisionError from an exact-cancellation duplicate-ticker merge is confirmed closed. Reproduced directly: create AAPL qty=100, then POST AAPL qty=-100 now returns 422 (Field(gt=0) rejects it before the merge division runs), never reaching the crash path. Since both merge operands are now schema-constrained > 0, their sum can't be <= 0 for finite inputs.

RESOLVED (was minor in the prior review pass): the TOCTOU race on the duplicate-ticker check is confirmed closed. Verified independently at the DB layer (bypassing the API entirely): two direct PositionORM inserts with the same ticker against the same engine raise sqlite3.IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: positions.ticker on the second commit. The resulting rare concurrent-insert 500 is explicitly decided as deferred, with rationale, in this task's decisions array.

RESOLVED (was minor in the prior review pass): the create_all lifespan stopgap is now documented as an interim state in docs/architecture/Backend.md §7, and db-migrations.json has a new checklist item + description note about needing `alembic stamp head` instead of a blind `upgrade head` against a pre-existing create_all'd database.

Non-blocking: PositionIn.ticker has no length/strip validation -- an empty string ("") is accepted and creates a position with that ticker, and a leading/trailing-whitespace ticker (e.g. " AAPL") is normalized only via .upper(), not .strip(), so it's treated as a different ticker from "AAPL" and creates a second row instead of merging. Both reproduced directly. Undermines the documented same-ticker-merges invariant for malformed-but-technically-valid input. Worth min_length=1 plus .strip() in the normalization step.

Non-blocking: unique=True on PositionORM.ticker is only applied by create_all to freshly created tables -- a database created before this PR won't retroactively gain the unique index. Already implicit in the documented create_all stopgap limitation, not new scope for this PR, but worth calling out alongside the existing stamp-head note once db-migrations picks this up.

Non-blocking, unaddressed carryover from the prior review pass: merge-averaging arithmetic (weighted avg cost, min(entry_date)) is still inlined in the router handler rather than a small pure function in app/portfolio/ (where risk.py/exits.py already live per Backend.md's module layout). Fine to leave for a follow-up.

review.notes:
Independent re-verification (not just trusting the fix-round report): reproduced the ZeroDivisionError-is-closed claim directly against a live TestClient (create AAPL qty=100, then POST AAPL qty=-100 -> 422 not 500); reproduced the unique-constraint claim directly at the DB layer bypassing the API (two direct PositionORM inserts for the same ticker -> IntegrityError on the second commit); regenerated backend/openapi.json locally via scripts/export_openapi.py and diffed byte-identical against the committed snapshot, and confirmed exclusiveMinimum: 0.0 is present on both quantity and avg_cost_basis in the committed schema. All three previously-flagged issues (ZeroDivisionError, TOCTOU race, undocumented create_all stopgap) are genuinely fixed. However the code-review skill (medium), run fresh against this fix round's diff, surfaced a new blocking gap in the same fix (Infinity bypasses gt=0 and produces a NaN avg_cost_basis that crashes db.commit() with an unhandled IntegrityError) which I independently reproduced -- see the blocking comment above. Backend coverage: 68 passed (up from 63 in the prior review pass -- the fix round's own regression tests), whole-repo 74.26% vs 72.44% pre-PR baseline on main (confirmed via a clean worktree) -- net improvement, not a regression; shortfall is pre-existing unimplemented stub modules unrelated to this PR. No ruff/mypy/lint config exists yet in backend/pyproject.toml -- nothing to run beyond pytest. No frontend exists yet, so the browser walkthrough step doesn't apply; noted explicitly rather than silently skipped. Findings posted as inline PR comment (schemas.py:117-118 / portfolio.py:70) and a summary review (gh pr review --comment, since --request-changes is blocked by GitHub on one's own PR, same as --approve).

Round 3 (this review): dispatched explicitly to hunt adversarially for another edge case in the same non-finite-float failure family rather than re-checking what rounds 1-2 already fixed. Found one: Field(gt=0, allow_inf_nan=False) has no upper bound, so two individually-valid finite floats (each passing validation on its own) can still overflow Python's float arithmetic to inf/nan inside the merge path in add_position -- reproduced live (POST quantity=avg_cost_basis=1e308 twice for the same ticker -> second call 500s with sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError: NOT NULL constraint failed: positions.avg_cost_basis, nan bound as NULL by sqlite3). This is the same crash signature as the round-2 finding but reached via a path neither round-2 fix (schema allow_inf_nan=False, or the RequestValidationError sanitizer) covers, since no RequestValidationError is ever raised here -- confirmed blocking. Also explicitly re-checked and confirmed clean: direct NaN (already tested), negative infinity (rejected), and every other numeric field in schemas.py (all response-only, no other client-supplied numeric input exists). Ran the full backend suite (77 passed, 0 regressions), confirmed backend/openapi.json is still byte-identical to a fresh `python scripts/export_openapi.py` regeneration, confirmed no ruff/mypy/eslint config exists anywhere in the repo (nothing beyond pytest to run), and confirmed no UI surface exists for this backend-only PR (browser walkthrough doesn't apply). Also ran the code-review skill (medium) in the background in parallel with a full manual line-by-line pass over the diff; its one finding (unique=True on PositionORM.ticker not retroactively applied by create_all to a pre-existing table) duplicates a limitation already flagged non-blocking in round 2 and covered by this task's create_all stopgap decision record, so it's recorded as a non-blocking carryover, not a new blocker. Findings posted as an inline PR comment (portfolio.py:66), a summary review (gh pr review --comment, since --request-changes is blocked by GitHub on one's own PR), and a follow-up PR comment for the code-review skill's non-blocking addendum.
